title: WhatsApp Web Now Supports Full Audio and Video Calling From Your Browser
excerpt: The update brings group calls, call transfers between devices, waiting rooms, and HD video to the browser-based client, eliminating the need for a desktop app.
body:
• WhatsApp has rolled out full audio and video calling on WhatsApp Web, including both one-on-one and group calls, directly from the browser.
  • New features include Call Transfer between devices, a Waiting Room for call links, QuickHD video, and noise suppression.
  • The update supports screen sharing, reactions, and a dedicated Calls tab with full call history in the browser.
  • All calls remain end-to-end encrypted using the Signal protocol, matching the security of mobile and desktop apps.

The Browser Becomes a Full Phone

WhatsApp has announced a significant upgrade to its web client, bringing full audio and video calling capabilities directly to the browser for the first time. The update, rolling out gradually, means users can now make and receive both one-on-one and group calls from WhatsApp Web without needing the desktop application.

The browser-based calling service includes features already available on other platforms — screen sharing, reactions, and a dedicated Calls tab showing full call history. For millions of users who spend their workday in a browser, particularly those on managed laptops that restrict app installations, the change eliminates a longstanding friction point.

New Features Across the Platform

The calling rollout comes alongside several other enhancements:

Call Transfer allows users to move an active group call from one device to another without hanging up — switching from phone to laptop, for instance, without disconnecting participants.

Waiting Room appears when creating a WhatsApp call link with approval required to join. Participants enter the waiting room until the host admits them, similar to features in Zoom and Google Meet.

QuickHD delivers high-definition video from the very first seconds of a call, rather than gradually improving quality as bandwidth stabilizes.

Noise Suppression removes background noise so voices come through clearly, even in loud or busy environments.

"The end-to-end encrypted web service will make it easier to jump on a call without leaving your browser."

— WhatsApp, official announcement

Security Unchanged

All calls on WhatsApp Web maintain end-to-end encryption using the Signal protocol, the same framework that protects messages, calls, and status updates across the platform. The browser version does not introduce any new security trade-offs compared to the mobile or desktop apps.

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

WhatsApp is the dominant communications platform for the Indian diaspora. An estimated 500 million Indians use the service, and for families split between continents, it is often the primary channel for daily voice and video calls.

The web calling feature is particularly useful for professionals who cannot install personal apps on corporate laptops but can access WhatsApp Web through a browser. It also fills a gap for Linux users, for whom WhatsApp has never offered an official desktop application.

WhatsApp said the features are rolling out gradually and will be available to everyone soon. The update builds on months of beta testing that began with one-on-one calling in February 2026 before expanding to the full feature set announced this week.
nri_angle: For the millions of Indian Americans who rely on WhatsApp as their primary link to family back home, browser-based calling means video calls with relatives in India without needing to install software on work laptops.
author: Diaspora Desk
